approach: Root cause (read): with `[parallel] max_concurrency = 2` (athena.toml:205; doc at config.rs:275-277) two jobs pass the dispatch disk gate (run/mod.rs:1088) while the disk is still empty, and each builds in its own folder `<job dir>/target`. Nothing orders those builds. A job's folder is not only `target/produce`: the baseline checks, the demonstrations and the verifier's `cargo` all leave a real `target/verify`, and everything goes only when the job closes. Fix: one build-folder slot, held from just before `baseline_stage` until the job is closed. `dispatch` (run/mod.rs) takes it after planning and before `resume_candidate` (1353) or `produce_and_verify` (1387). It drops it after `finish_dispatched`, and the guard's `Drop` first removes the job's `target/` and the holder file, then frees the lock. The slot is `slots::SlotQueue` with one entry over its own directory `<state>/build-folder/`. A second job reads and plans, then waits at the slot, with no hold, no attempt used and no discard. At dispatch a shortfall is not a hold only when free space plus the bytes under `target/` of the job that holds the slot meets the minimum; the holder is named in `<state>/build-folder/holder`. Every other low-disk case holds as today. Revision: (a) the folder wait is left out of `wall_time_execution_s` through a `RunClock` in `RunContext` (finding 2); (b) the credit counts only the slot holder (finding 4); (c) section 11 and D188 name the builds that stay outside the slot (finding 3); (d) run/mod.rs is justified as the only home of the producer-start path (finding 1). `max_concurrency` stays 2.

decisions.choice: Hold the build-folder slot for the whole of a job's build life: take it in `dispatch` after planning and before `baseline_stage` (before `resume_candidate` for a resumed job), and drop it after `finish_dispatched` has closed the job. The guard's `Drop` calls `StateDir::remove_target(job)` (state.rs:260, idempotent), removes the holder file, and only then lets the slot lock go (the slot field is declared last, so it drops last).
decisions.reason: Every build-environment site (producer.rs:197 and 360, checks.rs:484, 1034 and 1304, records_criteria.rs:820, verification.rs:243, mod.rs:2011) is reached only through `produce_and_verify` or `resume_candidate`, both called from `dispatch` (mod.rs:1353, 1387). One guard covers them all, and the resume path with them. The baseline and the verifier build in real `target/verify` folders, so the slot cannot be freed before the verifier. Removing `target` on drop makes 'slot free' mean 'no folder held' for held jobs too, whose job directory is not cleaned (close.rs:170-189 commits records only).

rejected.why: The baseline folder, the demonstrations and the verifier's `cargo test` still build in real `target/verify` folders afterwards, so job B's producer could build while job A's verifier does.

rejected.option: Take the slot a second time before the verifier
rejected.why: Job B could take it in between, so A's verifier would wait behind B's whole producer run. A's baseline folder would also be unprotected.
It misses the resume path and the folder removal done when the job closes.

decisions.choice: Implement the slot as `slots::SlotQueue::new(state.build_folder_dir(), 1, BUILD_FOLDER_WAIT, 600 s)` over `<state>/build-folder`, with a `BuildFolder` guard in disk.rs. After the acquire the guard writes the holder's job id to `<state>/build-folder/holder`. Before it queues, `take_build_folder` removes a holder file that names its own job (left by a crashed run).
decisions.reason: `SlotQueue` gives an exclusive file lock freed on drop or process death (slots.rs:5-9), first-in-first-out tickets, a `stop` callback on every poll for the kill switch (slots.rs:190-196) and cross-process tests. `try_slots` opens only `slot-N.lock` and `live_tickets` reads only `queue/` (slots.rs:221-290), so a `holder` file in the same directory is invisible to the queue. A separate directory keeps the count out of `max_check_slots` (slots.rs:143-152), whose slots are taken per cargo command by the producer's shim (producer.rs:377) and by every check (checks.rs:184).

rejected.option: Take `Class::Producer` from the existing `<state>/slots/` queue for the whole job
rejected.why: Its count is `max_check_slots` (default 1, config.rs:165), and the holder's own cargo shim and checks need that same slot, so the job would wait on itself.

rejected.option: A bare `try_lock` loop on a lock file
rejected.why: It re-implements ticket order, and with up to 16 workers (config.rs:269) a waiter could starve.

decisions.choice: At dispatch only, add `Athena::dispatch_disk_gate`. It runs `disk_gate` (idle-target sweep included). On a shortfall it adds `held` = `dir_bytes(<job dir>/target)` of the job named in the holder file, only when that job is not the asking job and its job lock is held (`job_lock_held`, state.rs:159). If `free + held >= required` it prints one `disk` line with the figures and returns `None`, so the job reads and plans and then waits at the slot. Otherwise it returns the `LowDisk` as today. The gates inside the run (mod.rs:1821, checks.rs:174 and 189, verification.rs:175, mod.rs:2344 and 2373) stay unchanged.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 4 of this round. A job lock is also held by `athena land` (landing.rs:853) and by manage commands (manage.rs:96), so counting every locked job could credit a `target/` that no slot holder will free. Naming the holder in a file the guard writes while it holds the lock, and requiring that job's lock to be held (a crashed holder has none), limits the credit to the one folder that returns to free space when the holder ends. A stale file that names a waiting retry of the same job is removed by that retry before it queues. The remaining case is a crashed holder whose job is locked by a manage command while another job dispatches: the cost is planner spend, because the pre-producer gate (mod.rs:1821) then holds the job. D188 states this. I use measured bytes, the same `dir_bytes` quantity `start_hold` counts (disk.rs:779-784), not the build-measurement T or `ESTIMATE_T_BYTES` (disk.rs:639, 6 GB), because the request puts a folder at 15-24 GB.

rejected.option: Count every other job whose job lock is held (the previous plan)
rejected.why: It credits a locked job that is not in the slot (finding 4).

rejected.option: Credit the expected folder size T instead of the real bytes
rejected.why: The 6 GB estimate is below the 15-24 GB folders the request names, and the holder's actual bytes are what free space regains.

rejected.option: Probe the slot (`try_acquire` or `waiting()`) and skip the gate whenever it is held
rejected.why: It blames any shortfall on the other job, and a `try_acquire` probe briefly takes the lock from a real waiter.

rejected.option: Set `max_concurrency` to 1 or check free disk only
rejected.why: That is the part 1 stopgap: it serialises reading and planning too.
It is a size estimate that holds the start, and it is off at the default of 1 (config.rs:164).

decisions.choice: The wait is bounded only by a 7-day `BUILD_FOLDER_WAIT` and the kill switch (`refuse_if_stopped`, lib.rs:301). A `SlotWait` from it goes through `hold_for_slot_wait` (close.rs:200), as the producer's slot wait does (mod.rs:1844-1847). Print the 'waiting' line from the `stop` closure on its second call, and print the time waited after the acquire when `slot.waited()`.
decisions.reason: `build_wait_s` (1800 s, config.rs:166) is shorter than one job's producer, checks and verifier together, and the request rules out a hold for waiting. The holder is bounded by its own deadlines. The `stop` closure runs before every attempt (slots.rs:195), so a line printed from its second call needs no probe and no change to slots.rs.

rejected.why: The second job would be held after 30 minutes.
It edits slots.rs, which is not a deliverable, for a line the `stop` closure already allows.

decisions.choice: No new config key, record type or `Stage`. The slot count is fixed at 1. A waiting job shows by its `disk` line in the job's log; agent-and-build-slots.md says how it looks in status.
decisions.reason: Out of scope forbids more than one slot. `reading_inputs` ignores `[parallel]` (config.rs:1354-1357). The stage board writes a row only when a stage is entered (`TableSink::enter`, drain.rs:940-952; `Stage` has four variants, state.rs:18-23), so a waiting job shows no row, like a job that is planning.

rejected.why: It changes `Stage::as_str`, the in-flight table and their tests, and the request does not ask for it.
It adds validation, a ceiling and tests for a count the design fixes.

decisions.choice: Leave the wait for the build folder out of `wall_time_execution_s`. `RunContext.clock` (mod.rs:1416, built at 1246 and 1325) becomes a small `RunClock { start: Instant, excluded: AtomicU64 }` with `elapsed()` = time since dispatch less the excluded time, and `exclude(Duration)`. `take_build_folder_or_hold` calls `ctx.clock.exclude(wait)` when the slot was waited for. It is a run-time value on the context, not a record field. The label in `totals()` (scoring.rs:124) becomes 'athena clock, from dispatch to the final verdict, less any wait for the build folder'.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 2. `wall_time_execution_s` is read in two places, `failure` (mod.rs:2518) and the verdict (verification.rs:457); both write `ctx.clock.elapsed().as_secs_f64()`, so they need no edit when `clock` keeps the method name `elapsed`. `failure` has 19 callers in six files and takes no `Closing` (mod.rs:2513), so the value cannot ride on `Closing` without changing them all; the context reaches both readers. The figure feeds two scored things (athena-score lib.rs:160-169 forecast quantiles, 330-336 scoring against the forecast). With the slot held to close, about half the jobs would wait through another job's whole build; recording that as execution time would skew both. Before this change no job waited at all, so the past series holds no such wait and stays comparable. No past record is recomputed: the gate rescoring reads the stored value (athena-gate jobs.rs:142-147). An `AtomicU64` (nanoseconds) keeps `RunContext` usable across threads.

rejected.option: Keep the wait in the figure and say so in D188
rejected.why: The finding shows it skews the forecast and its scoring, and the owner should not have to read a long wait as slow execution.

rejected.option: Carry the wait on `Closing` and subtract at the two sites
rejected.why: `failure` has no `Closing` parameter and 19 callers, and it would also edit verification.rs, which is not a deliverable.

rejected.option: Add a record field for the wait
rejected.why: It changes a record schema and needs round-trip and `AnyRecord` coverage for a value only the run reads.

risks.risk: Throughput: with the slot held from baseline to close, `max_concurrency = 2` overlaps only reading and planning, not builds.
risks.mitigation: That is what the request asks (one folder holder at a time). D188 and the CHANGELOG say so. The wait is bounded by the holder's own deadlines and the 7-day limit.

risks.risk: Deadlock between the build-folder queue, the check slots and the repository lock.
risks.mitigation: Slot setup and removal are plain file locks and a `remove_target`. The wait comes after planning, when the job holds no check slot and no repository lock, and `take_build_folder` runs before `baseline_stage` takes any check slot. The tests run the two-jobs-in-threads shape.

risks.risk: Removing `target` when a held job's guard drops could lose work a retry needs.
risks.mitigation: A held job keeps its candidate and resume mark outside its job directory (state.rs:289-296), so the retry rebuilds. `remove_target` is idempotent. The held-before-the-producer case in the criterion-3 test asserts the folder is gone.

risks.risk: A job that is short on disk for its own reasons while the holder's folder exists plans before it is held, which spends planner money. The credit can also be wrong when a crashed holder's job is locked by a manage command (the holder file is stale but names a locked job).
risks.mitigation: The credit counts only the named slot holder with a held job lock, so `athena land` or a manage command on another job cannot trigger it. The `disk` credit line names the figures. The post-acquire gate (mod.rs:1821) still holds a job that is short for another reason, before its producer, so the cost is planner spend, not a wrong build. The counter test shows a hold when the holder's folder does not explain the shortfall. D188 names the planner spend.

risks.risk: The wall-time figure of a job that waited drops by the wait, so it differs from the figure a job would have had before this change.
risks.mitigation: Before this change no job waited at all, so the past series holds no folder wait and stays comparable. Only the run-time reading changes: athena-score and athena-gate read the stored number, no record is recomputed, and the forecast and scoring code is untouched. There is no records-based demonstration to run; the criterion-1 test compares the stored value with the test's own `Instant`, an independent source.

risks.risk: A very long wait occupies a drain worker.
risks.mitigation: A job's `go` blocks on the queue, so the drain counts it as a worker in flight while it waits. The 7-day limit and the kill switch end it, and a `SlotWait` becomes a hold with no attempt used, the existing path at mod.rs:1844-1847. The 7-day mapping is shared with that path and is not run in a test, because a 7-day wait cannot be simulated.

risks.risk: Thread-timing flakiness in the whole-run tests.
risks.mitigation: Every wait in the new tests is a bounded poll on observable state (queue `waiting()`, file existence, an atomic) with a 10 s bound, as run/tests.rs:6420 does. The one 300 ms sleep only sets a lower bound for the wait that the wall-time assertion subtracts; no sleep decides a result by racing.

risks.risk: The decision-log link check (D187) fails on D188's wording.
risks.mitigation: D188 uses no `Amends` or `Supersedes` phrase. The producer runs `cargo test -p athena-core governed` and `cargo test -p athena-cli --test backtest` and fixes the wording if a check names it.

risks.risk: Part 1 may already have changed line 205 or its comment in the base.
risks.mitigation: The producer reads the base's athena.toml first. If it has 1 on line 205, set it to 2 and keep exactly three comment lines above `[parallel]`.

risks.risk: Two big builds stay outside the slot: the drain's self-rebuild after a landing and the check slots' warm target directories, so free space can fall below the gate with two jobs although only one holds a job folder.
risks.mitigation: Not changed in this job (no code change is asked for, and the request keeps the slot count and cleanup out of scope). Section 11 and D188 name both, and the Host open question asks for their disk use. The gates inside the run still hold a job whose free space falls short.

demonstrations.method: One core test over two real `Athena::go` calls on two scoped threads, as the drain's workers call it (drain.rs:4705-4721). The repository is `repo_with_planning(1)`, so both jobs plan. The check is a command that writes a file into `$CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, so the real baseline leaves a real `target/verify`. The planner script of each job marks itself inside planning and waits (10 s bound) until both are inside. The producer wrapper logs start and end. The first producer waits (10 s bound) for a waiter on the folder queue, then sleeps 300 ms, so the second job's wait is at least 300 ms. The verifier wrapper logs and writes `target/verify/blob`. A sampler thread polls `jobs/*/target/*` every 2 ms and counts jobs that have a real (non-link) directory there. The test times each `go` with its own `Instant`.
demonstrations.observes: Both planners were inside planning at once. The log reads first-start, first-end, first-verifier, second-start. The first producer saw a waiter. The peak number of jobs holding a real build folder is 1. Both jobs end `Finished` with state Landed; neither returned `LowDisk` or `SlotWait`, and neither has a hold marker. The second job's stored `totals.wall_time_execution` value plus 0.3 s is at most its own measured `go` time (the folder wait is left out), and the first job's value is positive.
demonstrations.fails_without: Remove the `take_build_folder` call in `dispatch`: the first producer waits its bound for a waiter that never appears, `second-start` comes before `first-end`, and the peak holders is 2, so the log, waiter and peak assertions fail. Remove `ctx.clock.exclude(..)`: the second job's `wall_time_execution` is about its whole `go` time less a few milliseconds, so the 0.3 s assertion fails.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point `Athena::go` (run/mod.rs `go_job` -> `dispatch` -> `produce_and_verify`; the job lock is taken at mod.rs:456). Fixture: `athena_with` (run/tests.rs:191) with `repo_with_planning(1)` (293), a new check constant that writes into `$CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, `crate::test_support::plenty_of_space`, and a script that wraps the planning script with `counting(counts, Some(root))` (3114) and `each_job_its_own_edit` (6579). The wrappers only block, log and write files; they hold none of the gate or the clock. The queue probe is `build_folder_queue(&athena.state)` and `RunClock` is the clock, both added by this plan (steps 3 and 4). Every other piece exists today.

demonstrations.method: Two tests with a simulated disk. The free-space function is `capacity` minus the file lengths summed by its own walker over `<root>/jobs/*/target` (an independent walker, not `dir_bytes`), minus a ballast file in the second test. Test one: capacity 12 GB, minimum 10 GB. Job A's producer writes a sparse 8 GB file under `target/produce` and waits (10 s bound) for a waiter on the folder queue; the main thread starts job B's `go` once that file exists. Test two (`a_job_short_of_disk_for_its_own_reasons_is_still_held_at_dispatch`): capacity 12 GB, A's folder 2 GB, and A's producer also writes a 5 GB ballast file in the state root and removes it only after B's `go` has returned.
demonstrations.observes: Test one: free space is 4 GB (below 10 GB) while A builds. B prints the `disk` credit line, which names A as the holder, and no `held` line. B stays queued at the folder, then starts after A's close and lands. B's `read_hold` is None. A also lands with no hold marker, because B owns no folder while A builds. Test two: B's `go` returns `LowDisk` with free 5 GB, the `held       environment: low disk` line is printed, and B's hold marker exists. B's producer never ran. A lands once the ballast is gone. A third unit test in disk.rs (`the_credit_counts_only_the_slot_holder`) shows a locked job that is not named in the holder file adds 0 bytes, and so does a holder file naming a job whose lock is free.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without `dispatch_disk_gate`, B's `go` returns `LowDisk` at the dispatch gate (mod.rs:1088) and the test's `expect` fails. Without the slot, B's producer starts inside A's window and A's producer never sees a waiter. If the credit counted every locked job, or counted unconditionally, the second test and the holder test fail.
demonstrations.seam: Entry point `Athena::go` on two threads. Fixture: `athena_with(.., free_space_fn, script)` (191). The new `fn(&Path) -> io::Result<u64>` free-space functions are injected through `StateDir::with_free_space` (state.rs:233), modelled on `low_once_marked` (6758). The producer wrapper around `counting` writes the sparse files. The credit lives in `dispatch_disk_gate` and the holder file in `BuildFolder`, both added by plan step 3; the doubles hold none of it.

demonstrations.method: For each ending, run job one through `go`, assert the folder queue is free (`take_slot_soon`, 6433) with `waiting() == 0`, that `jobs/<id>/target` is gone and that the holder file is gone, then run a second job to Landed. Endings: landed (`PASSES`); rejected (`FAILS_ON_EDIT`, 104); failed with no change (a producer that edits nothing, the empty-diff failure in `no_change_reason`); held for low disk before the producer (`low_once_marked`, as the test at 6234); and the kill switch set through `registry().stop_file()` while the job waits for a folder a probe holds, which returns an error with no ticket left. A separate test, `a_resumed_job_takes_the_build_folder_before_its_checks`, repeats the setup of the test that ends at 6406: it holds a job for low disk before its checks, holds the folder with a probe, runs the retry's `go` on a thread and asserts no check ran while the probe holds. After the probe drops the job resumes and lands.
demonstrations.observes: After each ending the slot is free, the queue is empty, the job's build folder and the holder file are gone, and the next job proceeds. The resumed job's checks start only after the folder is free. The code has no job state named discard (no match in lib.rs, state.rs, disk.rs, run/mod.rs, run/close.rs, store.rs or manage.rs); rejected, failed, held and killed are the not-landed endings.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the guard were leaked (forgotten, or dropped only on the success path), the next `try_acquire` stays `None` and the following job's `go` hangs past the test's 10 s bound. If the `Drop` did not remove `target`, the absence assertion fails for the held and killed endings.
demonstrations.seam: Entry points `Athena::go` and `Athena::retry`. Fixture: `athena_with`, `PASSES`, `FAILS_ON_EDIT`, `low_once_marked`, `counting`, `check_seam` (the thread-local fake check, used at 6488), `registry().stop_file()` (used at run/tests.rs:686). A probe holder comes from `build_folder_queue(&athena.state).try_acquire()`, as `slot_queue` is used at 6409 and 6787. All exist except `build_folder_queue`, added in step 3.
